title: Claims Manual: Term Life Insurance Death Claims and Proceeds
content:
## Coverage on the date of death

A Term Life Insurance death claim is covered when the policy was in force or in its grace period on the insured's date of death. A death on or after the lapse date of a lapsed policy, or after expiry or termination, is not covered and no claim is registered.

## Conditions of disbursement

- Death proceeds are disbursed only on a death claim whose certified death certificate has been received and whose request status is approved.
- Disbursement proceeds only while the policy status on record is death claim pending or claim paid.

## Contestable and suicide periods

When the date of death is within the product's contestability period of the issue date — or within that period of the reinstatement date for a reinstated policy — the claim is approved only after contestable review; the claims committee may rescind the contract for material misrepresentation, and a rescinded or denied claim refunds the premiums paid. When death is by suicide within the product's suicide exclusion period of the issue date, the benefit is limited to the premiums paid.

## Gross proceeds

Otherwise the gross proceeds are the face amount
- plus the accidental death benefit rider amount when the death was an accident and the insured was below the product's accidental death rider expiry age,
- less any installments overdue at death,
- less the outstanding acceleration lien,
- plus, where the product refunds unearned premium on death (every tier does), premium paid for any period beyond the policy month of death.

Interest is added to each payee's share at the product's death claim interest rate, simple, for the actual calendar days from the date of death to the disbursement date over 365, rounded to the cent.

## Payees

Proceeds are divided among the surviving primary beneficiaries of the designation in effect on the date of death in proportion to their shares. The share of a primary who died before the insured passes to the surviving primaries pro rata; if no primary survives, to the contingents on the same basis; if none survives, to the owner, or the owner's estate when the owner is the insured. A share payable to a beneficiary younger than the product's minor age is paid only to a court-appointed guardian or UTMA custodian. A payee whose share is at least the product's Beneficiary Access Account minimum may elect an Ashgrove Beneficiary Access Account; smaller shares are paid by check or direct deposit.

### Worked example (hypothetical, non-accidental death, no suicide or contestable issue)

Face 250000.00; one installment of 45.00 overdue at death; lien 0.00; unearned premium 0.00. Gross proceeds: 250000.00 less 45.00, which is 249955.00. Two surviving primaries at 60% and 40% receive 149973.00 and 99982.00 before interest. At 3.5% for 73 days, the 60% share earns 149973.00 times 0.035 times 73 over 365, which is 1049.81.

### Re-allocation example (hypothetical)

Primaries A 50%, B 30%, C 20%; B died before the insured. B's 30% passes to A and C pro rata (5 to 2): A receives 50% plus 21.43%, C 20% plus 8.57%, that is about 71.43% and 28.57% of the proceeds.
